newsitem.title: FRANCE: BA's French carriers, unions near accord.
newsitem.headline: BA's French carriers, unions near accord.

text.p: British Airways' French airlines TAT and Air Liberte and unions representing most of the cockpit crew members are close to an agreement to end a two-week strike, a union official said on Tuesday.

"We drafted a preliminary agreement that the SNOMAC, SPAC, UNAC and SNPNAC, members of the USPNT trade union, are ready to sign," said an official with the USPNT, which represents around 60 percent of the pilots and navigators at the airlines.
He said the SNPL, which represents the other 40 percent, did not want to sign the accord, which sets rest periods and would provide a traditional 13th month's pay to Air Liberte staff.
The accord provides for 8.75 rest days each month and nine days beginning in November. The unions had asked for 10 days.
"We're not very satisfied with the agreement. We're not signing it," said an SNPL spokesman. He declined to say whether the union would maintain its strike call.

Around half the TAT-Air Liberte flights have been grounded in the past two weeks by cockpit crew striking to protest against BA's move to run the airlines as a single entity ahead of a proposed full-fledged merger. BA took over Air Liberte in January after the French carrier became insolvent.
